Repair command for profiler, metrics, and tree views of catchup and repair.

# Purpose
This file implements the `repair` command for Firedancer. It provides a standalone application that can run in profiler mode, metrics mode, or tree mode. In profiler mode, [`repair_topo`](<#repair_topo>) builds a reduced topology that includes the tiles, workspaces, links, and shared objects needed to measure repair and catchup behavior. It sets CPU affinity, creates the `repair` tile and related tiles such as `shred`, `gossip`, `sign`, and `scap`, and connects them with the required network and shared-memory links. It also configures special shared objects such as `fec_sets`, `poh_shred`, and `root_slot`, then finalizes the topology and applies the normal Firedancer configuration steps.

The file also contains the command handlers that use this topology at run time. [`repair_cmd_fn_profiler_mode`](<#repair_cmd_fn_profiler_mode>) starts the reduced topology and prints repair metrics, request counts, latency histograms, and slot progress until catchup completes. [`repair_cmd_fn_metrics_mode`](<#repair_cmd_fn_metrics_mode>) joins a running instance and prints live repair metrics, peer latency data, and catchup slot information, while [`repair_cmd_fn_tree_mode`](<#repair_cmd_fn_tree_mode>) prints the repair forest state. The file also parses command-line options such as `--manifest-path`, `--metrics`, `--tree`, and `--iptable-path`, and it defines the `fd_action_repair` action so the command can be registered in the Firedancer command framework.
